To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relative orientation of the CBM and catalytic domain of fungal glucoamyles can vary and is not influenced by ligand binding.
the relative orientations between the CBM of fungal glucoamyles and their catalytic domain are flexible and that the flexibility of these domains is not influenced by the presence of starch.
the orientation between CBM and catalytic domain of fungal glucoamyleases is not static, but flexible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of glucoamylase and the interaction between the catalytic domain and the starch-binding domains.
the structural analysis of enzymes that are of industrial relevance and are involved in the degradation of starch biomass.
the structural basis of enzyme-substrate interactions in glucoamylase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative orientations of the CBM and catalytic domains are flexible, but the exact mechanism of how this influences the activity of glucoamylase remains to be elucidated.
the CBMs are flexible and can be oriented in different ways relative to the catalytic domains, which can be important for the interaction of the enzymes with the polymeric substrates.

the CBM of the glucoamylase does not have a rigid position relative to the catalytic domain and that the CBM does not have a specific function in substrate binding, which is a major difference to the starch-degrading enzyme amylase.

the CBM and catalytic domain of glucoamylase are flexible with respect to each another and the CBM can bind to the catalytic domain in two different orientations.
the flexibility of the starch binding domain in the glucoamylase is a result of a lack of interaction between the domains, which allows the CBM to adopt a variety of orientations.
